lines: Oh, fuck! My pocket just ripped off. Again!
Look at your jeans. See those tiny metal dots on the pockets?
Those are rivets. And no, they're not decoration, you little fashion goblin.
Almost every pair of jeans on Earth has them. Including the ones you're wearing right now.
And today... I'm deleting them! Every single rivet!
Now you shove your phone in your pocket. Rrrip! The corner tears wide open.
Congratulations. Your pants are now a skirt with commitment issues.
Pocket corners take the most stress. Every time you jam your hands in, the seam gets yanked apart.
A rivet pins those corners together with metal, so the fabric can't tear.
Workers kept ripping their pants. So a tailor named Jacob Davis hammered copper rivets into the corners.
But he was too broke to pay for the patent. So he teamed up with the guy who sold him the fabric. Levi Strauss.
On May twentieth, [1873|eighteen seventy-three], they got the patent. And blue jeans were born.
So the most famous pants in history exist because one guy couldn't afford paperwork. Relatable.
And you thought those dots were bling? Buddy, they're older than your great-great-grandma.
Next time you put your hands in your pockets, thank a broke tailor.
So... what should I delete next?
